newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Tarkett, Sommer merging floor business.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Tarkett, Sommer merging floor business.

text.p: Germany's Tarkett AG and French plastics group Sommer Allibert SA said on Wednesday they would merge their floor covering businesses to create a global company.

Under the deal, which has yet to be approved by competition authorities and shareholders, Sommer Allibert will take a 60 percent stake in Tarkett through a public takeover offer of 32.75 marks ($19.23) per share, a premium of 0.65 marks over Tuesday's closing price.
In turn, Tarket will buy Sommer's floor coverings business for 705 million marks in cash. The transaction does not include Sommer's floor coverings for motor vehicles.
The merger will create a company called "Tarkett-Sommer" which will have annual sales of 2.6 billion marks
"This transaction is an important step in creating a truly global flooring company," Tarkett chief executive Lars Wilsen said in a statement.
"It should lead to significant benefits to both businesses, their customers, employees and shareholders."
Tarkett's shares rose 12 percent in floor trading, a jump of 3.90 marks to 36 by 1015 GMT.
Sommer-Allibert shares initially rose strongly, too, but later fell 1.56 percent to 214.50 francs as the Paris bourse plunged more than 3.7 percent.
The transaction will result in a significant reduction in in the 65 percent shareholding in Tarkett owned by investment funds affiliated to Doughty Hanson and Goldman Sachs Capital Partners.
Both Tarkett and Sommer Allibert predicted the transaction would boost net earnings.
Sommer Allibert will buy 20.1 million shares representing 60 percent of existing Tarkett capital or 50 percent when fully diluted for the exercise of warrants to be issued.

In order to ensure that Sommer Allibert will own 20.1 million shares, investment funds affiliated with Doughty Hanson and Goldman Sachs Capital Partners have agreed to sell Sommer Allibert the shortfall between the number of shares tendered and 20.1 million shares.
Tarkett said it planned to finance the 705 million-mark payment by taking up 504 million in debt and by issuing a warrant bond for 201 million marks.

The warrant bond will be offered in denominations of 30 marks and will pay a fixed annual coupon that will be 0.80 percentage point above the yield of the most recent five-year government bond, or Bundesobligation, Tarkett said.
The transaction is subject to approval from competition authorities, satisfactory due diligence and approval by the supervisory boards and by shareholders.

"The combination of these two companies will create a global floor covering producer with a well-balanced portfolio of activities, both from a geographic and a product point of view," Sommer and Tarkett said in a joint statement.

Sommer Allibert said it was Europe's leading plastics processor with sales of 14 billion French francs ($2.4 billion) and 16,000 employees worldwide. It main business area are automotive equpment and coverings, as well as home furniture, handling and packaging for the cosmetics industry.
Sommer's floor coverings business employs 4,300 people and in 1996 generated a turnover of 4.4 billion French francs, generating an operating profit of about 420 million francs before goodwill.
Tarkett in 1996 had sales of 1.3 billion marks and operating profit of 136 million marks.
--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
($ = 1.702 German Marks)
($ = 5.753 French Francs)
